messages.content: Predict this person's actual contribution in an anonymous repeated four-person public-goods game. The four members remain the same. In each interaction every member gets a fresh 20 points and simultaneously contributes an integer from 0 to 20 to the group, keeping the remainder. The experimenter doubles all four contributions and divides that sum equally among four. Each person's ordinary earnings are 20 minus own contribution plus that equal share. The instructions say fractional shares are rounded to the nearest whole point (.5 upward), and teach 33 points for a 32.5 point share. No stopping horizon has been announced. Apply only the rules already explained to you. After each interaction a table shows all four contributions, private remainders, the share and ordinary earnings.  No cumulative totals are displayed. Communication is disabled and identities are anonymous. All task 2 points count toward payment at 1 point = 1 JPY, with an additional 100 JPY participation payment and course credit. The earlier hypothetical allocation-preference task did not affect pay. The supplied earlier preference choices are in original question order; option 1/2 amounts are [self,other] hypothetical JPY, not game points. Own expected-others reports concern the mean contribution of the other three people after the latest rule notice; they were not rewarded for accuracy and are not actual others' choices. Quiz answers were followed by corrective explanations. The original quiz answers were not retained in the available record, so they are not reconstructed or treated as personal ability. Prior peer trajectories are an anonymous unordered multiset, with each trajectory kept linked across its past interactions. Original A/B/C display ordering was not exported; the ordering here is a canonical order based only on past contributions, not a claimed A/B/C mapping. Exact historical payoff display values were not exported, so only contributions and private remainders are reproduced; you can apply the announced payoff rule. Output only one integer from 0 to 20, the points contributed now, without explanation.
